prize_parts.citation: for optical lattice clocks at the magic wavelength

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from B023 to B043. Optical lattice clocks embody a clear and fundamental atomic-physics advance: the magic-wavelength lattice permits many atoms to be confined and interrogated without the trapping field spoiling the clock transition. This converted an apparent trade-off between confinement and accuracy into a controllable quantum measurement system. The result has been reproduced independently over many years and has demonstrated a new regime of time- and frequency-resolved tests. Katori's defining concept and Ye's decisive experimental development form a compact, physically intelligible attribution.
statement.case_against: The citation must not blur optical lattice clocks into the whole history of atomic clocks or treat a future redefinition of the second as its validation. A final historical review must also test whether Katori and Ye alone encompass contributions inseparable from the magic-wavelength architecture and its defining realization.

responses.point: Johansson argued that the strongest case for B043 is the magic-wavelength lattice as a controllable many-atom quantum system, rather than simply improved clock performance.
responses.response: I agree. That framing identifies the underlying physics and makes the case stronger than one based only on metrological figures of merit. It is precisely the controlled preservation of the atomic transition in an optical trap that makes the achievement a distinct advance.

responses.point: Kroll emphasized the independent reproducibility and sharply bounded attribution of B043, while questioning whether B023 has reached a similarly clear endpoint because scalable fault-tolerant computation remains unresolved.
responses.response: This comparison has changed my judgment. Trapped-ion experiments have achieved remarkable control and quantum simulation, but the boundary between their foundational protocols, the broad experimental lineage, and the still-unachieved computing objective remains less clean. B043 has already delivered its central physical capability repeatedly, without relying on a promised future outcome.

responses.point: Mehlig regarded B043 as a compelling mature achievement but preferred the exact universal structure of two-dimensional conformal field theory over a precision-measurement advance.
responses.response: The exact theoretical achievement is formidable, but I give greater weight here to a new quantum measurement capability whose physical principle, experimental realization, and independent validation can all be bounded precisely. B043 is not merely an incremental improvement within metrology.

uncertainties: Whether archival review supports limiting credit for the magic-wavelength lattice-clock breakthrough to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye.
How narrowly the final citation must be drawn to distinguish this achievement from earlier atomic-clock and optical-frequency-metrology advances.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
